app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

note.description: Note is the site's own marker, such as nE or Absetzung.

result_qualifier.description: ResultQualifier says how a result was reached when it was not simply played out.

rounds.description: Rounds lists the rounds of a cup or tournament; pass a round id as competition_id to read that round alone.

note.description: Note is the site's own marker, such as nE or Absetzung.

result_qualifier.description: ResultQualifier says how a result was reached when it was not simply played out.

round.description: Round is the round of a cup or tournament match, such as 1. Hauptrunde.

rounds.description: Rounds lists the rounds of a cup or tournament; pass a round id as competition_id to read that round.

open.description: Open reports whether the page shows the round's matches inline.

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Returns a page of one of the ten Top-Amateurstatistiken rankings (Kreisklasse to Regionalliga, championship matches): top teams by goals, goal ratio, goals against and points average, highest-scoring matches, biggest draws, and top scorers by goals, ratio and goals in one match per week or season. Filter by season, team type and federation and page with `limit` and `offset`. A ranking is bounded to roughly its top 200 entries; `final` marks the last page.

get.description: Searches FUSSBALL.DE clubs by club name, postcode or place, or both (both must match), and returns each club's id, name, postal code, city and logo. The first page reports the `total` hit count; page with `limit` (1 to 100, default 20) and `offset`, and `final` marks the last page. Zero results is a valid response. The site's search is not fuzzy and matches a club's official name (for example `RasenBallsport Leipzig`, `SC Freiburg`), so a looser display name such as `RB Leipzig` can return nothing: search by place or one distinctive word, or use the `club_id` that every team, table and match row already carries.

get.description: Returns the matches FUSSBALL.DE's Matchkalender lists around a five-digit postcode within a date range (default today plus six days, at most 92 days), optionally filtered by team types and competition kind. Each match includes its team type (for example D-Junioren) and league. The upstream returns at most 10 matches per request and has no paging: `truncated` is true when the page is full, so narrow the dates or filters to see the rest. Zero matches is a valid response.

get.description: Returns every match of a competition's season (fixtures and results), including the earliest matchdays, optionally filtered to one team and a date window; the date window is applied by the site, so a narrow window is cheaper than filtering a full season. Cups and tournaments are assembled round by round: every match carries its `round` and the response lists the `rounds` with their ids. Use it for a complete schedule; use `fussballde-matchday` for one matchday.

get.description: Returns the matches of a competition's current matchday, of a numbered matchday (`matchday`, 1 to the competition's matchday count, reported as `matchday_count`) or of the matchday around a date. Each match has teams, date, kick-off time, score and status (`finished`, `scheduled`, `cancelled` and the other values listed below). Cups and tournaments have no numbered matchdays; for them the response lists the competition's `rounds` (each round id works as `competition_id` to read that round) and labels every match with its `round`. Dates, times and scores are decoded from the site's obfuscated glyph fonts.

parameters.name: date
